paras: The shooting of Hawthorne took place in early September 1881 in Boon township, Columbia County, Arkansas, when men deputized to arrest Hawthorne, a Black man accused of stealing corn, shot him with buckshot and squirrel shot as he fled. He survived and was held in the county jail to await the grand jury. The only known report is a short local item in the Magnolia Columbia Banner.

According to the Columbia Banner, Esq. Baily of Boon township issued a writ of arrest against Hawthorne, identified as "(col.)," on a charge of stealing corn. Constable Locket and Geo Starnes went to make the arrest, but Hawthorne fled.

Starnes, Montgomery, Smith and "two negroes" were then deputized to make the arrest, and Hawthorne fled a second time. In the paper's account, Starnes fired his gun into the air to frighten him into stopping, and Hawthorne instead turned and fired three shots at one of the Black deputies. Starnes, Smith and the other Black deputy then fired at him, "lodging buck and squirrel shot enough in his body to bring him to the ground." The brief gives no place, time of day or description of his wounds, and no one else is reported hurt.
Hawthorne was jailed, "awaiting the action of the Grand Jury." No report of grand jury action, a trial or his recovery appears in the coverage.

The Columbia Banner ran the story on 15 September 1881 among its local items under the headline "Shot and in Jail." The item calls Hawthorne "the rogue" and tells the story from the deputies' side, with his flight and his shots presented as fact and no version from Hawthorne. No other paper, white or Black, is known to have carried the story.

reader.title: Shooting of Hawthorne
bases: A constable's deputized party shot and wounded Hawthorne while trying to arrest him on a writ, and he survived and was jailed (A1); the group was a posse, but none of the posse types fits a non-fatal arrest shooting.
One local brief in the county paper is the only report found (A1); the next week's issue does not mention the case (A2).

acts.note: Constable and Starnes tried to arrest on a writ; Hawthorne fled.
Deputized party pursued him; he fled a second time.
Buck and squirrel shot lodged in his body, bringing him down, after he allegedly fired three shots at a Black deputy.
Jailed to await the grand jury; jail place not stated.
